title: Perfect cohomology models descend to rational and common field stages
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ with structure map $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the raw rationalized and common finite-stage coefficient categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], and ordinary and compact-support point complexes as in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], with their ordinary module derived duals [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with $E\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every $K_E\in D^b_c(X,E)$ and every integral representative $K_R\in D^b_c(X,R)$, where $R=\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $K_R$ belongs to the uniform finite-Tor category [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. There exist bounded finite projective $R$-complexes $P_*,P_!$ representing $R\Gamma(X,K_R)$ and $R\Gamma_c(X,K_R)$ such that the rational point complexes are represented respectively by $P_*\otimes_RE$ and $P_!\otimes_RE$, and their duals by the finite-dimensional signed dual complexes. Consequently all four rational point complexes have bounded finite-dimensional cohomology. For every $K\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$, there is a finite field of definition $E'\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, an object $K_{E'}\in D^b_c(X,E')$ representing $K$, and bounded complexes $C'_*,C'_!$ of finite-dimensional $E'$-vector spaces representing $R\Gamma(X,K_{E'})$ and $R\Gamma_c(X,K_{E'})$. In the common-stage point category [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category], $R\Gamma(X,K)$, $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ and their duals are the objects $(E',C'_*)$, $(E',C'_!)$, $(E',C_*'^{\vee})$ and $(E',C_!'^{\vee})$, the duals being the signed dual complexes formed at the stage $E'$. Their cohomology spaces $\mathrm H^i(C')\otimes_{E'}\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules] are finite-dimensional over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and vanish outside a finite interval. No Weil structure, properness, or smoothness is assumed.

proof.text: Use integral_residue_tor to put the supplied integral representative in the uniform finite-Tor category. Obtain a finite dimension bound for X. Apply integralSections_perfect_reduction to its ordinary and compact section objects.

Apply the proved small_perfect_coefficient_lift to each of the two perfect section objects. This gives small bounded finite-projective complexes P_s and P_e and their canonical coefficient/carrier-lift presentations.

Apply sections_rational_model_comparison to each presentation and the given representative isomorphism. Obtain the ordinary and compact rational models E tensor_R P_s and E tensor_R P_e. Scalar extension preserves strict support and finite generation, and every vector space is projective.

For either field model apply projective_hom_evaluation_model with target the coefficient unit complex, then transport the source through its model isomorphism and the target through the derived unit comparison. This gives the two displayed signed Hom models. The existing perfect-complex theorem makes the dual of a perfect field complex perfect; its finite homology and cohomological bounds give pointFiniteDimensional for both objects and both duals.

Keep the actual finite stage F=K.stage and its rational object K.obj. The ordinary and compact point fibres at the small Shrink coefficient field already have bounded finite-dimensional cohomology by their full-subcategory membership. Exact extension along Shrink.algEquiv preserves that property. Apply DerivedCategory.isPerfect_iff and the bounded finite-projective definition to choose ordered bounded field models C_s and C_e. The normalized object formula of pointQbarFibre identifies the two point images with these same-stage models. This uses the existing point-fibre finiteness interface rather than constructing integral models a second time.

source.place: Step 3, finite-dimensional field complexes and scalar extension

proof.text: The signed Hom complex into F[0] has degree i the ordinary linear dual of C^{-i}; it has finite-dimensional terms and strict bounds [-b,-a]. Apply the beta-isomorphism clause of perfect_dual_scalar_calculus for F -> Omega, the projective Hom evaluation model over Omega, and the exact scalar-extension comparison with Q. The resulting isomorphism identifies the derived dual of each realized model with the realization of its signed dual at F. Transport along the ordinary and compact point-category presentation isomorphisms.

source.place: Step 3, finite-dimensional field complexes and scalar extension

proof.text: Every one of the four stage objects has bounded finite-dimensional cohomology. The coefficientQbarCohomology object formula is exact scalar extension of its cohomology. Its existing finite-dimensionality theorem gives finiteness; extension preserves zero objects. Induct over the finite set of the four stage objects, taking the minimum lower bound and maximum upper bound, starting with [0,0] for the empty set. This gives one ordered interval and proves all the final cohomology assertions.
